name: Monport GPro Vision
tagline: Split fiber with 16 MP camera and autofocus: 50W standard or 60W, 100W and 200W MOPA
tldr: Monport's GPro Vision, launched in June 2026, is a split (open galvo) fiber laser with a 16 MP positioning camera and autofocus. Four sources: 50W standard ($4,249, 200 × 200 mm field), 60W MOPA ($5,299), 100W MOPA ($6,919.99) and 200W MOPA ($8,599, 22,000 mm/s), the MOPA tiers on a 175 × 175 mm field. Open a tier for exact specs.
mainObjective: Camera-aligned metal marking, colour marking and engraving

priceRange.note: Official Monport store, Oct 2026: 50W $4,249, 60W MOPA $5,299, 100W MOPA $6,919.99, 200W MOPA $8,599; the LightBurn Pro bundle adds $200

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

cutExample.description: Not a sheet cutter: thin metal only, in many passes

cut: Thin brass, copper and steel sheet (many passes)
cannot: Clear glass or acrylic marking (needs UV or CO₂)
Parts larger than the galvo field without repositioning

pros: 16 MP camera for visual placement and batch layouts on every tier, with autofocus
Choice of sources from a 50W standard fiber to a 200W MOPA, on the same chassis design
LightBurn and SapphireMark support on Windows and macOS
cons: Open split galvo with a Class 4 beam: an enclosure or strict eye protection is required
Costs more than Monport's camera-less GT series at each comparable power
Launched in June 2026: no independent review yet

faq.question: Which GPro Vision tiers can do colour marking?
faq.answer: The 60W, 100W and 200W tiers use MOPA sources, whose adjustable pulse width produces controlled oxide colours on stainless steel and titanium. Monport's launch announcement describes the 50W as a standard fiber laser, so it is the tier for black, white and deep marks rather than colour.

faq.question: How does the GPro Vision differ from Monport's GT series?
faq.answer: Both are split fiber lasers with autofocus. The GPro Vision adds a 16 MP camera for visual placement, batch layouts and Monport's conveyor accessory, and costs a few hundred dollars more at each comparable power.

standoutFeatures.title: Camera on a split fiber
standoutFeatures.body: A 16 MP camera shows the part on screen so artwork can be placed directly on it, which most split fiber lasers at this price leave to red-dot framing.

standoutFeatures.title: Four sources, one design
standoutFeatures.body: From a 50W standard fiber for tags and tools to a 200W MOPA for production engraving, all with the same camera and autofocus.

beginnerNotes: This overview covers the whole GPro Vision line. Choose the 50W for bare-metal marking without colour, the 60W MOPA for colour and fine work, and the 100W or 200W MOPA when depth and throughput pay the bills.
proTips: Calibrate the camera with the supplied sheets before batch work and confirm with a test mark. Plan an enclosure and fume extraction before the machine arrives.
primaryUse: Split fiber laser with camera placement for metal marking and engraving.

editorialDepth.advantages: The GPro Vision brings camera placement, usually found on enclosed desktop galvos, to Monport's split fiber format, with autofocus and a source range wide enough to cover gift shops and small production lines alike.
editorialDepth.limitations: Every tier costs more than its camera-less GT counterpart, the open design needs an enclosure or strict eye protection, and the specs are Monport's until independent reviews appear.
